isolation_policy: bubblewrap mount namespace: only the workspace, the policy-accepted read allowlist and the opencode runtime exist; the repository, the other arms' results, the earlier sessions and the global opencode configuration (its MCP servers and plugins) are not mounted; plus the opencode v2 permission object (bash denied, edit and write denied, read and external_directory deny-by-default with the explicit allowlist)
limitations: The mount namespace is the filesystem guarantee; the model provider is reachable over the shared network, so a model that was shown a file can still send it away.
sandbox_argv:
This exploration produces ONE mechanism. You are one of three independent reviewers; you see the same frozen evidence bundle and the same proposals as the others, and you do not coordinate with them before handing in.
THE RESEARCH OBJECTIVE:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.
THE SCOPE CONTRACT (a proposal that misses it is sent back, not scored):
A proposal is IN SCOPE only when all of this holds:
  1. BEHAVIOUR: it names one training-only behaviour signal (directed item transitions, user-interest branching, sequential co-consumption, popularity-adjusted graph neighbours, behaviour-conditioned assignment weights, ...) and says how it is computed.
  2. HYPERBOLIC GEOMETRY: it names an explicit curved operation (trainable or fixed negative curvature, Poincare or Lorentz distance, exp/log maps, geodesic scoring, curved residual, curved quantization, curved regularization) and where in training or quantization it acts.
  3. REAL COUPLING: one connected computational pathway uses both, so that removing either changes the core computation. A behaviour suffix on an unchanged Euclidean quantizer, a standalone hyperbolic loss beside an unrelated behaviour loss, a geometry name without geometric computation, or inherited unused hyperbolic code do NOT qualify.
  4. TESTABLE EFFECT: it states what should observably change (SID assignment, gradient or parameter update, prefix behaviour predictability, or Stage3 Recall) and names the behaviour-off, geometry-off/Euclidean and both-on comparisons. The three switches must be part of the mechanism, so that the coupling can be shown to be real, but the round RUNS no ablation arm: each candidate is trained once.
  5. MINIMAL SPECIFICATION: equations or pseudocode, inputs and outputs, numerical safeguards and the training cost. No proof and no paper section are required.
SID quality (ER, prefix counts, collisions) is NOT a scope criterion and NOT an admission rule.

EXPERIMENT POLICY (binding on every proposal, implementation and review):
  - ONE candidate, ONE training run, on the frozen budget (3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards, the frozen Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping).
  - NO ablation experiments: the behaviour-off, geometry-off and both-on switches must EXIST in the code and must be correct, but no arm is trained with them switched off.
  - NO tuning experiments: no sweep over the coupling weight, the clip bound, the temperature, the usage weight or any other constant. A constant that enters the mechanism has to be DERIVED (a scale-relative bound, a measured quantity, a documented default), not chosen by trying values.
  - NO multi-seed experiments: a candidate is not repeated with other seeds, so a single run decides it and the seed noise is part of the uncertainty.
  - The behavioural diagnostics (coherence, adjacency, transfer predictability) are recorded, never used as an admission gate; Stage 3 test_recall@10 is the judgement.
  - A proposal that needs an ablation, a sweep or a seed repetition to make its case is out of programme: it has to make the case with one run.
THE SELECTION POLICY (rank-2026-10-v1): the reviewers RANK the proposals. The proposal the reviewers place best, in total, is the round's mechanism. Rank every proposal, best first, and give each one a reason that names the evidence you used.
Read the frozen evidence bundle for each proposal before you place it: a placement you cannot ground in the evidence is not a placement.
Write PLAIN TEXT, one line per proposal, in exactly this shape:
RANK: <idea_id> | position=<1 for the best, then 2, 3, ...> | reason=<one line>
RANK: <idea_id> | position=<n> | reason=<one line>
Every proposal must appear exactly once, the positions must be 1..N with no ties and no gaps, and the reason must say what in the evidence put the proposal there. If you cannot ground a proposal in the evidence, rank it last and say so in its reason; do not leave a proposal out.
THE PROPOSALS:
IDEA: TOLLCAP-SID
TITLE: Behaviour-funded hyperbolic toll gate on a capacity-frozen SID transport (shape A: partition provably untouched, only cell membership of noise-floor items changes).
MOTIVATION: All three negative rounds lost recall by moving the objects the quantizer owns: round one bent the residual chain, round two displaced 99.1% of items off the text geometry, round three added a fourth argmin-pinned level. Recall tracked distance-from-text-geometry, not prefix capacity. So the remaining degree of freedom that has NOT been tested is cell MEMBERSHIP: the SID vocabulary, the codebooks and every prefix count can be held bit-identical while the assignment of a small set of boundary items to those existing cells is re-decided. This proposal takes shape (A) explicitly: it acts at quantization time, after the frozen Stage-2 RQ-VAE, as a capacity-frozen optimal transport inside each level-1 group in which a curved distance sets the toll of a relabel and the training-only successor PPMI decides whether the toll is worth paying.
NOVELTY: No earlier proposal here prices a relabel with a hyperbolic distance. Existing mechanisms move embeddings (geodesic shift to successor barycentres), move codebooks (Poincare-Frechet successor updates), change radial coordinates (context-entropy radial assignment), add cones, add levels, or set per-level curvature from transition scores. TOLLCAP-SID changes none of those: alpha, the codebooks, the cell set, the cell sizes and the token vocabulary are frozen and asserted equal to the baseline; the only things that can change are which existing cell a noise-floor item is named by. Curvature is load-bearing in exactly the one way the round's own measurements say is real - the radius/compactness term - because the Poincare chord factor 1/(1-||m_s||^2) makes entering a fine, boundary cell cost more than entering a central cell, so the curved metric acts as a price on the transport rather than as a displacement. It therefore cannot repeat prefix merging (counts frozen exactly), moving the input off the text geometry (codebooks and embeddings untouched, per-item toll bounded by the quantizer's own RMS error), or a fourth argmin level (no new level, no new token, identical SID vocabulary).
CHANGE: Replace the plain nearest-cell rule for a bounded set of boundary items by a capacity-frozen transport inside each level-1 group, where a move's cost is its Poincare distance increase minus lambda times its successor-PPMI advantage, and lambda = eps_rec/sigma_A is derived, not tuned.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': "(1) Freeze everything: text embeddings x_i, level codebooks C1..C3, baseline triple t(i)=(a,b,d), cell set S, and per-cell sizes n_s. All of these are read-only.\n(2) alpha = 1/max_i ||x_i||; phi(x) = tanh(alpha||x||) * x/||x|| (unit Poincare ball, curvature -1 fixed, scale derived from the data, no curvature knob).\n(3) d_P(p,q) = arcosh(1 + 2||p-q||^2/((1-||p||^2)(1-||q||^2))), evaluated in float64.\n(4) Cell centroid m_s = phi(c1_a + c2_b + c3_d) for s=(a,b,d), fixed for the whole pass.\n(5) eps_rec = sqrt(mean_i d_P(phi(x_i), m_t(i))^2), the quantizer's own noise floor.\n(6) Training-only behaviour: A(i,s) = log((p(s|i)+eps_p)/(pi(s)+eps_p)) from directed consecutive training transitions, p(s|i)=sum_{j in s} p(j|i), pi(s)=sum_{j in s} q_j with q the global incoming share, eps_p = 1/(total transitions).\n(7) lambda = eps_rec / sigma_A, sigma_A = std of {A(i,s): s in the same L1 group, s != t(i)}.\n(8) Cost and admissibility, per item i and candidate cell s in the SAME level-1 group:\n    toll(i,s) = d_P(phi(x_i), m_s) - d_P(phi(x_i), m_t(i));\n    Delta(i,s) = toll(i,s) - lambda*(A(i,s) - A(i,t(i))); Delta(i,t(i)) = 0;\n    admissible iff toll(i,s) <= eps_rec; items with zero outgoing training transitions get A=0 everywhere and never move.\n(9) Per level-1 group: expand each cell into n_s slots (so capacities are exactly the baseline sizes), build the square matrix M[i,slot]=Delta(i,s)+1e-9*1[s != t(i)], solve with scipy linear_sum_assignment in float64, decompose the item permutation into cycles, keep cycles in ascending order of max toll while the cumulative moved count stays <= 0.05*N, and set t'(i)=t(sigma(i)). Dropping whole cycles keeps every capacity exact.\n(10) Emit t'(i) plus a record: rho, per-cycle tolls, prefix counts at levels 1/2/3 before and after, behaviour contrast before and after."}
COST: Zero added work per Stage-2 step (24556 items, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs = 72,000 steps, unchanged 0.145-0.16 s/epoch) and zero added Stage-3 work. One pass: one sparse pass over the training transition pairs (seconds), 24556 hyperbolic distances plus ~700 per level-1 group, and 251 linear_sum_assignment calls of size ~98x98 (about 7.5e7 flops). Total well under one minute once, i.e. ~0.3-0.8 ms amortized per Stage-2 step, under 1% of the frozen Stage-2 wall clock.
HYPOTHESIS: Worth keeping if moving boundary items into behaviourally coherent existing cells raises prefix behaviour predictability and therefore Stage-3 recall, because the text-geometry signal the baseline relies on is preserved at the quantizer's own resolution. Observation: rho small but non-zero, prefix counts and SID vocabulary identical, training-split behaviour contrast strictly higher than baseline, and test_recall@10 above 0.0679. Falsified if rho>0 and contrast rises while recall does not move, or if rho=0 (the shell is empty) and the SIDs are identical to the baseline.
RISKS: ['The admissible shell may be empty because the PPMI advantage rarely pays an eps_rec toll, giving a null result equal to the baseline. Or the PPMI advantage is dominated by popularity so moves concentrate in hub cells, which the cycle cap limits but does not eliminate. Or behaviour contrast rises on the training transition graph yet does not transfer to the beam-search predictor. Also, a relabel can move an item to a cell whose Stage-3 token statistics are already saturated by 11-item collisions, diluting the benefit.']
END IDEA

IDEA: HCAUDIT-SID
TITLE: Null-calibrated hyperbolic contrast audit that repairs at most five percent of SID assignments inside a measured prefix guard
MOTIVATION: SHAPE (A). Three rounds moved the many (curved residual 0.05439; global geodesic pull of 99.1% of items 0.05165; global extra PPMI level 0.04823) and lost monotonically with distance from the plain text geometry, not with prefix count. Behaviour CONTRAST is the only diagnostic that predicts recall (+0.7104 plain, +0.7170 Euclidean control) while Gromov-delta weighting and ancestor-depth weighting hurt (+0.12, +0.075 wrongly signed). So this mechanism freezes the encoder, adds no level, pulls nothing to a barycentre, uses no Gromov delta and no ancestor depth, and repairs only the statistically demonstrable tail where text geometry and behaviour contrast disagree, with level-1 and per-level prefix drift measured and bounded.
NOVELTY: Unlike round 1 (curved residual chain), round 2 (global popularity-adjusted successor barycentre), round 3 (extra PPMI-direction level pinned by argmin), poincare-frechet-successor-codebook (successor-weighted Frechet codebook), CURVCTRL-SID (level curvature from prefix-transition score) and BRad-RQ (behaviour-ranked radial assignment), this never re-ranks or moves the bulk. It audits at most 5% of 24556 items; the eligible set is fixed by a degree-stratified permutation null on behaviour contrast; the target codeword is chosen inside one Lorentzian score containing both behaviour affinity and curved distance; the budget is emergent from the null; the guard is measured; curvature is a gauge fixed by a data quantile, so there is nothing to tune.
CHANGE: At the end of frozen Stage 2, build train-only successor-PPMI profiles, select items whose contrast with their level-1 subtree is significant under a degree-conserving permutation null, and re-quantize only those items (<=5% of 24556) with one score: z-scored behaviour affinity to the candidate subtree profile minus z-scored Lorentz distance to the candidate cumulative reconstruction, under a checked and reported prefix guard.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'N=24556, L=4, K codebook size per level; h_i frozen Stage-2 encoder output; e(l,k) level-l codebook vector; c(i,l) baseline codeword; r(i,l)=sum_{m<=l} e(m,c(i,m)). From TRAIN sequences only: successor counts N_ij, top-50 PPMI vectors b_i (L2), subtree profiles beta(l,k)=L2(mean_{j:prefix_l(j)=k} b_j). Eligibility g_i=max_{k!=c(i,1)} cos(b_i,beta(1,k))-cos(b_i,beta(1,c(i,1))); null = 20 permutations of b inside outgoing-degree deciles; tau = 99.5th percentile of pooled null g (documented 0.5% false-positive convention); eligible iff g_i>tau and total behavioural degree d_i>=20. Rank by d_i*g_i descending, B_max=floor(0.05N). Curvature gauge c0=1/q99({||h_i||} U {||e(l,k)||})^2. Map x~=exp_0^{c0}(x). Score s(i,l,k)=zhat_k[cos(b_i,beta(l,k))]-zhat_k[d_{c0}(x~(h_i),x~(r(i,l-1)+e(l,k)))/R_l], R_l = median baseline d_{c0}(x~(h_i),x~(r(i,l))) floored at 1e-3, zhat per-item z-score over k with sigma floor 1e-6. For a selected item greedy l=1..L: k*=argmax_{k used} s(i,l,k); flip only if s(i,l,k*)>s(i,l,c(i,l)); else keep baseline codeword and residual. Guard: level-1 count total variation <=0.05; distinct used prefix counts each level within +/-5% of baseline; changed level-1 tokens <=0.05N. On failure drop the lowest d_i*g_i item and recompute (<=B_max times). Export repaired SID table to the frozen Stage-3 protocol.'}
COST: Per training step at the frozen scale: 0 added work; 24 steps/epoch x 3000 epochs unchanged at 0.145-0.16 s/epoch (435-480 s). Audit once at export: 4*N*K <= 1.0e8 score evaluations after 24556+4K exp maps and 4K subtree profiles, about 1-10 GPU-seconds (1-2 CPU-minutes), under 0.2% of Stage-2 wall clock; guard bisection <=1227 histogram recomputations; Stage 3 unchanged. Total added wall clock under 1 minute.
HYPOTHESIS: Worth keeping iff (i) mean behaviour contrast between an item and its prefix-siblings falls on the audited tail (train-only), (ii) Euclidean-versus-hyperbolic target disagreement is non-trivial so geometry is not a gauge artifact, and (iii) one frozen Stage-3 run reaches test_recall@10 > 0.065 (realistically above the untouched 0.0679). If only 1-2% repair and recall is flat within seed noise, the idea fails and is recorded negative with its number.
RISKS: ['The eligible tail may be too small to move Stage 3; the null may reject almost everything; flips may land on low-degree items Stage 3 rarely sees; the level-1 guard may force B to zero; behaviour affinity may be dominated by a few large subtrees; hyperbolic and Euclidean rankings may agree almost everywhere, leaving geometry decorative. Each is measured and reported.']
END IDEA

IDEA: SHELL-CURV-RQ
TITLE: Margin-shell curved behaviour re-assignment: at most 5% of items may be re-tokenised, and only the Poincare distance to behaviour code-centroids decides among near-tied codes.
MOTIVATION: Rounds 1-3 showed that moving the SID partition toward behaviour costs recall monotonically, and that the loss grows with distance from the plain text geometry. But a codebook's Voronoi boundary is exactly where the text embedding is genuinely ambiguous; those items carry a SID that is arbitrary with respect to behaviour. Fixing only that thin shell keeps 95% of the text-geometry partition intact while making the remaining ties behaviour-consistent, which is the cheapest place to buy prefix predictability.
NOVELTY: Unlike behaviour-weighted Sinkhorn, curved residual chains, successor barycentre shifts and a fourth argmin level, this mechanism never moves the encoder, never updates the codebooks, never adds a level and never relocates a non-tied item. Behaviour acts only as a tie-break inside a hard 5% margin budget, and curvature acts as a bounded displacement budget through exp_0, so neither can drag the whole partition off the text geometry.
CHANGE: After the usual Euclidean RQ-VAE assignment pass, take the per-level margin shell containing the smallest 5% of nearest-vs-second-nearest gaps, recompute level-l behaviour centroids from train transitions, and let the Poincare distance from each shell item's behaviour point to those centroids choose the code among the shell candidates instead of the Euclidean argmin.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': "See SPEC EQUATIONS. Inputs: text embeddings x_i for 24556 train items, L=3 codebooks of 256 codes each, train-only directed transition matrix. For each level, form the shell, compute q_k as a tangent-space Frechet mean, pick the code minimising d_c(b_i,q_k), keep straight-through gradients as in the base RQ-VAE. The budget B=0.05 is the round's stated guard, not a tuned value; delta_l is the B-quantile of the measured margin distribution."}
COST: One extra bulk pass per epoch (24556x256 top-2 margins at all 3 levels, plus Poincare distances for about 1228 shell items per level), roughly 0.9M artanh evaluations per epoch, about 10-30 ms on one card, under 2% of the 0.145-0.16 s epoch; at 24 steps per epoch that is under 0.1 ms per step, so 3000 epochs add under 90 s wall clock. The PPMI behaviour points are built once before training.
HYPOTHESIS: If the margin-shell items are the ones whose SID is behaviourally arbitrary, replacing their code with the curved behaviour-consistent candidate raises prefix behaviour predictability in the recorded train diagnostics and Stage3 test_recall@10 holds at or above the 0.0679 baseline and above the 0.065 gate, while level-1 agreement with the baseline assignment stays >=0.95 and prefix counts stay within a few percent of 251/1769/2201. Observed through the per-level flip count and the recorded prefix counts.
RISKS: ['5% may be too few flips to move recall beyond seed noise; the shell may be dominated by rare items with thin behaviour statistics, making flips noisy; the behaviour centroids may be unstable early in training (mitigated by origin fallback and the >=5-member rule); the curved ranking may coincide with the Euclidean ranking, which is a genuine possible negative that the geometry-off switch is designed to expose.']
END IDEA

IDEA: BEHTIE-SNAP
TITLE: Curvature-scaled hyperbolic behaviour-contrast snap of one existing RQ level inside a measured quantisation-error tie band.
MOTIVATION: Three rounds lost recall by moving item codes (curved residual, successor barycentre, PPMI fourth level), and the loss tracks deviation from the frozen text geometry rather than prefix count; meanwhile the programme's own 107-pair measurement says behaviour CONTRAST is the positive predictor of recall (+0.7104). The missing mechanism is one that raises the behaviour contrast of the SID assignment while moving nothing off the text geometry beyond the quantiser's own error scale, and that adds no level, deletes no code and creates no residual cascade.
NOVELTY: Earlier mechanisms here changed the quantiser input (curved residual chain), shifted the input toward a popularity-adjusted successor barycentre, added an argmin-pinned fourth level, ranked items radially by context entropy, or updated codebooks with successor-weighted Frechet means. This candidate freezes the trained encoder and every codebook, runs once after Stage 2 as a deterministic 24,556-item pass, and edits exactly ONE coordinate of ONE existing level for the items inside a tie band as wide as that level's own median squared quantisation error. The curved part is a Poincare-ball geodesic comparison of popularity-adjusted transition profiles, with curvature fixed by the measured radial scale of those profiles, so radial (peakedness/popularity) differences are compressed and only behaviour DIRECTION separates codes. No new codebook, no new level, no removed code, no gradient term.
CHANGE: For each item, form the admissible set of existing level-l codes whose squared text distance to the item's encoder output is within rho_l of its current best code, then pick the code minimising a two-term dimensionless objective: normalised text distortion (weight 0.5) minus hyperbolic behaviour-contrast similarity (weight 0.5). Deeper codes are kept stale (their residual chain is not recomputed), so the edit is a single-coordinate relabelling with no cascade.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': "(1) From the Stage-2 TRAIN split only, count directed transitions C_ij = adjacent pairs (i then j) in training sessions; p_ij = C_ij / sum_j' C_ij'; q_j = column share of C; PPMI_ij = max(0, log(p_ij/q_j)); x_i = L2-normalised PPMI row truncated to its top M = 20 successors (20 is the frozen Stage-3 beam width, a documented default, not tuned). (2) b_i = V_64^T x_i with V_64 the top-64 right singular vectors of the PPMI matrix from a truncated SVD with a fixed start vector (deterministic, no seed sweep); items with no outgoing train transitions get b_i = 0. (3) Curvature from data: R = 95th percentile of ||b_i||, kappa = artanh(0.9)/R, c = kappa^2, so the ball has fixed curvature -c and the 95th-percentile profile sits at Poincare radius 0.9; b~_i = exp_0^c(b_i) = tanh(kappa||b_i||) b_i/(kappa||b_i||); code behaviour centroid mu_k = mean_{i in code k} b_i (tangent barycentre), c~_k = exp_0^c(mu_k). (4) rho_l = median over train items of ||z_i - c_{k(i)}||^2 at level l; A_i = { k : ||z_i - c_k||^2 <= ||z_i - c_{k(i)}||^2 + rho_l }, capped to the 32 nearest codes (documented default). (5) sigma_k = mean_{i in k} d_P(b~_i, c~_k); S_i(k) = exp(-d_P(b~_i,c~_k)/sigma_k) in (0,1]. (6) J_i(k) = 0.5*||z_i - c_k||^2/rho_l - 0.5*S_i(k); k*(i) = argmin_{k in A_i} J_i(k), ties keep k(i). (7) The edited level is l = argmax over l >= 2 of the measured behaviour impurity 1 - mean_k mean_{i in k} cos(x_i, xbar_k), so level 1 can never be edited."}
COST: zero added FLOPs inside the 72,000 Stage-2 steps (24 steps/epoch x 3000 epochs), and Stage 3 is untouched. One post-hoc pass: counting train transitions O(E) over the train interaction stream; one rank-64 truncated SVD of the 24,556 x 24,556 sparse PPMI matrix (order 0.5M non-zeros) taking minutes on one CPU node; centroids and geodesics O(N*K_l*d_b) ~ 24,556 x 2,201 x 64 ~ 3.5 GFLOP, under a second on one GPU; the snap itself O(N*32*(d_b+d)) ~ 75 MFLOP. Total added wall clock a few minutes, under 2 percent of the Stage-2 run; per-step cost at the frozen scale is exactly 0.
HYPOTHESIS: If items that share a prefix but lead to the same popularity-adjusted successors make one SID coordinate predictable from that prefix in Stage 3, then reassigning items only among near-tied text codes raises that coordinate's behaviour contrast, lowers Stage-3 conditional entropy at that position, and lifts test_recall@10 above 0.065 without the deviation penalty. Worth keeping only if intra-code contrast of the snapped level rises AND text-distortion inflation stays within one median quantisation error AND the Stage-3 entropy at that position falls; at parity the mechanism is inert and the band occupancy is the evidence.
RISKS: ['the tie band may be nearly empty at the chosen level, making the arm bit-identical to the baseline (recorded parity, with the occupancy as the measurement); the geodesic may prefer radially extreme codes and create singleton deep prefixes (counted and reported); the stale residual makes the reconstruction inconsistent for moved items although Stage 3 never reads it; the contrast gain may not survive seed noise; the positive contrast correlation may be cross-sectional rather than causal.']
END IDEA
